pageCache.pageTitle: Vision, Ethos & Values | Field End Infant School
pageCache.text:
Vision, Ethos & Values
FEIS Vision: Developing Aspirational Lifelong Learners Who Will Help To Shape The Future
We believe in encouraging our children to develop their aspirations, to know they can be who they want to be and have dreams for the future. We have a broad curriculum to develop our children’s talents through physical, musical and creative activities while retaining a strong provision in the core subjects of English, mathematics and science. We want to encourage our children to develop enquiring minds and the skills to ensure they are lifelong learners in whatever path they choose. We support all children to build relationships, developing emotional skills and learning how to make good choices to prepare for their futures.
We use our Field End Infants 'Learning Superheroes' to teach children how to approach learning effectively. Each embodies an aspect that we feel is essential in helping children to develop a positive attitude to learning and a growth mindset. We use the language of learning in our praise, looking for opportunities to reward children when they have concentrated, cooperated, used their imagination, been daring or taken risks in their learning and, importantly, when they have had fun in their learning!
FEI's 'LEARN' Values
These are core values that we hold which, we believe, make the school a safe and happy environment in which everyone is able to learn harmoniously. We teach children to take responsibility for being a good role model to others and to live out these values as members of our school community.
British Values at Field End Infants
We are proud to be a multi-cultural community, made up of different faiths and ethnicities, who are also British citizens with a duty to uphold the fundamental British values of democracy, rule of law, mutual respect and tolerance and individual liberty. We actively look for ways to teach children about these, through assemblies and through highlighting their relevance to our everyday school lives. Below are a few of the ways in which we help children to understand these.
Tolerance of different Faiths and Beliefs

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher | Field End Infant School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Field End Infant School and to our website. We hope that you will find this website helpful whether your child already attends our school or if you are considering joining us.
As a longstanding member of staff (I started as a teaching student in 2002 and joined the leadership team in 2009, before becoming headteacher in 2022), I have seen the school go through many changes- in government, in education policy and in curriculum to name just a few- but what has never changed is the sense of community and feeling of belonging you get from being a member of staff here.
We have always strived to ensure that this sense of belonging extends to our children, families and the community we serve; that Field End feels like a ‘home from home.’ As headteacher, I am committed to preserving this ethos; I believe that children learn best when they feel safe, happy and cared for and when school and families work in partnership.
Our school vision centres around ‘Developing aspirational lifelong learners who will help to shape the future.’ For us, this means helping pupils to become self-motivated, independent learners with a wide range of knowledge and skills that will be useful to them throughout their lives. We are proud of the important part we play in laying the foundations for children to live happy, fulfilled lives and excited to work with you to shape the very best education and school experience for children.

Welcome from our PTA
FOFE (Friends of Field End) is our schools PTA (Parent Teachers Association), to which you are automatically a member the moment your child enrolled into what is now their second home of Learning, education, diversity and fun. We welcome you to tap into your hidden talents to help enhance our current program and support our children.
Our aim is to organise a varied calendar of events that will put a smile on every child’s face after their hard day working in class, ranging from discos, summer and Christmas fayres, workshops and trips.
We are always looking for parents/carers to volunteers at events, become class reps and share your knowledge, experience and skills. Getting involves enables you to meet other parents, make new friends and support FOFE in continuing to deliver an action packed programs every year.
Your support is always appreciated, from wrapping gifts at home, to volunteering an event. We appreciate that childcare is often a concern for parents wanting to get involved in school activities, and therefore remind you as school is an extension of our family life, ALL children are welcome.
Check out our upcoming events at: Friends of Field End Infants FoFE (pta-events.co.uk)

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Designated Safeguarding Lead & Deputy | Field End Infant School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Designated Safeguarding Lead & Deputy
At Field End Infants, we recognise that, in order for a child to be ready and able to learn, they must feel physically and psychologically safe and that their emotional needs must be met. As Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) and Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL), we have responsibility for supporting our staff in ensuring that our children are safe and happy at school.
We work closely with staff to ensure that all safeguarding and child protection policies are in place and adhered to. This involves working with all school stakeholders, including staff, governors, parents, volunteers and children to ensure that everyone understands what we must do in order to keep our children safe.
We also ensure that the school complies with its statutory obligations to follow the Prevent Strategy, identifying and safeguarding children who may be vulnerable to radicalisation by extremist groups.
Mrs. Butler, in her role as Attendance Champion works closely with Mrs. Killeen, our Attendance Officer to support us in this role by identifying children for whom attendance is becoming an issue. They explore how to remove barriers to attendance by working with our families.
We also prioritise the mental health of our staff. We have a member of staff currently training as a Mental Health Lead to support staff in looking after their own wellbeing and that of our children.
Should you wish to find out more about aspects of wellbeing we may be able to support you with, please contact the school via email (office@fieldendinfants.co.uk) or phone (02088666163). We would be pleased to answer any questions you may have.
Mrs. V Jarvis & Mrs. C Page
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) & Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL)

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the SENDCo
The role of the special educational needs and/or disabilities coordinator (SENDCo) is to coordinate inclusion across the school and support early identification and interventions for children with special educational needs.
Partnerships with parents and carers play a key role in enabling us to create an inclusive, nurturing environment. We recognise that parents ad carers hold key information and have knowledge and experience to contribute to the shared view of a child's needs and the best ways of supporting them. We actively encourage parents and carers to discuss any concerns they have about their child’s development with staff.
Since 2009, we have continuously been awarded the Inclusion Quality Mark “IQM Inclusive School Award” This is nationally recognised award that provides external validation of our inclusive practice and ongoing commitment to developing education inclusion in our school. Since 2021 we have also been awarded the “IQM Centre of Excellence Award.”
Should you wish to find out more about our provision for children with special educational needs and / or disabilities, please contact the school via email (office@fieldendinfants.co.uk) or phone (02088666163). We would be pleased to answer any questions you may have.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Year Group Leads | Field End Infant School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Year Group Leads
At Field End Infant School, pupil attainment is at the heart of all we do. As year group leads, we have responsibility for overseeing teaching, learning and assessment across each year group to ensure that our teaching is founded in current thinking about best practice in education and that we continually evaluate and review teaching practices to ensure they are enabling children to make the best progress possible.
Evaluation of children’s learning involves ongoing assessment. Teachers observe children’s progress across the curriculum in order to gain information that will help them make decisions about how best to move learning forwards. This may involve providing extra support within a lesson, or through targeted interventions in addition to whole class input. It may also involve planning learning activities that increase challenge.
Several times a year, teachers make a summative judgement about children’s progress towards end of year age related expectations. Part of our role involves analysing the data this generates, allowing the school to spot trends and quickly ascertain where our strengths lie and where we need to target support in order to enable children to make rapid progress, particularly where they are at risk of falling behind. We engage with parents and carers at these key points to help them understand how they can support this process at home and also with school governors, who play an important role in holding the school accountable for the attainment and progress of the children we teach.
Our curriculum and teaching approaches are constantly evolving in line with best practice, but you can find out more about them by clicking on our ‘F.E.I.S Journey’ tab.
Should you wish to speak to us about teaching and learning at Field End Infants, please contact the school via email (office@fieldendinfants.co.uk) or phone (02088666163). We would be pleased to answer any questions you may have.
Mrs. A. Lavender (Nursery Lead)
Ms. M. Feldman (Reception Lead)
Miss K. Morris (Year One Lead)
Mrs. C Bedford (Year Two Lead)

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery After School Wraparound Care | Field End Infant School
pageCache.text:
Nursery After School Wraparound Care
Nursery wraparound care is run by Nursery staff. Staff are DBS checked, with early years staffing ratios observed. A first aider and member of the Senior Leadership Team is present onsite for the duration of the session.
Sessions cost £22.50 per day for two year olds and £16.85 per day for three and four year olds. Sessions run from 3:30pm until 5:45pm and are non- refundable. We offer regular and casual bookings. You may enquire in person via the school office, or by emailing office@fieldendinfants.co.uk
Half termly invoices will be emailed to you, stating the sessions attended and the amount to be paid.
All bookings are subject to availability and minimum numbers and a place cannot be guaranteed.
For consistency, children will have access to the activities they have been familiar with throughout the day. On top of this, they will be encouraged to ask for extra toys / puzzles / activities that they would like to explore and engage with.
Extra focused activities are planned for, including food preparation and craft activities.
Children will take part in additional after school snack time, where we will continue to work on their independent feeding and fine motor skills.
Please note that the last collection time from wraparound is 17:45 to enable staff to leave promptly and for the Nursery to be cleaned. Late arrivals after this will incur a charge of £5 for each five minute increment and parents / carers who persistently arrive late may have their child’s right to attend revoked.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast club | Field End Infant School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast club
As part of our wrap around care, we provide a Breakfast Club before school at a cost of £4.00 per day for children in Reception, Year One and Year Two. For Nursery, the daily charge is £7.50 for 2 year olds or £5.65 for three and four year olds. This provides a warm, welcoming atmosphere in which the children may enjoy a shared, relaxed, sociable breakfast; consisting of a choice of healthy cereals, toast, tea, fruit juice and water. Making us aware of any difficulties your child may have with eating is helpful.
After eating, children are encouraged to explore the activities before the beginning of the school day, such as toys, games, puzzles and books. Children may complete homework if they wish to, but no adult help or supervision with homework can be given.
The children will be supervised until the start of the school day, as follows: a. Juniors – will be escorted onto the playground from 8.40am where there is a member of staff on duty b. Reception, Year One and Year Two – will be escorted to their classrooms at 8.45am
c. Nursery - will be delivered by parents to the Nursery building and remain there until the beginning of the school day
Payment The cost per day must be paid each month in advance. No refunds will be made for late arrivals or non-attendance including sickness.
Breakfast Club runs from 7.45am until the beginning of the school day.
Admissions The criteria for admissions will be on the following basis 1st - Children requiring 5 mornings per week 2nd - Children requiring 4 mornings per week 3rd - Children requiring 3 mornings per week 4th - Children requiring 2 mornings per week 5th - Children requiring 1 mornings per week Should there be a situation where place has become available and 2 children on the waiting list are eligible, siblings will be prioritised.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reduction of Published Admissions Numbers | Field End Infant School
pageCache.text:
Reduction of Published Admissions Numbers
As parents / carers were advised in our October newsletter, we have been reviewing our class organisation to ensure we continue to meet the needs of local pupils and families effectively. The school’s current Published Admissions Number (PAN) is 90, but overall pupil numbers have declined over the past four years. This reflects both a reduction in local families and a wider drop in birth rates across Greater London.
In response, the school’s governors and officers at Hillingdon Council are considering it may be sensible to formally reduce the Reception PAN to 60, starting from the September 2027 intake. This adjustment would help the school to plan staffing and class sizes more effectively, allowing us to focus resources where they’re most needed and continue providing high-quality education for local children. This proposed change will not affect current pupils, their siblings, or other families seeking a place at the school in the future.
If you have any questions, please speak to the Headteacher or contact the Hillingdon admissions team at admissions@hillingdon.gov.uk.
Please note: if the number of local families increases significantly in the future, the school and council could choose to reinstate the additional 30 places for a year group, Increasing the PAN can be done immediately and does not require consultation, unlike a reduction. This consultation will be run in parallel with Field End Junior School’s consultation on their proposal to reduce their PAN from 90 to 60, effective from September 2027.
Community Schools Admissions Arrangements
As set out in the School Admissions Code, Admission authorities must set (‘determine’) admission arrangements annually. Where changes are proposed to admission arrangements, the admission authority must first publicly consult on those arrangements. Consultation must be for a minimum of 6 weeks and must take place between 1st October and 31st January of the school year before those arrangements are to apply.
Hillingdon Council is the admissions authority for all Hillingdon Community schools and the Council will be consulting for 6 weeks from 9am Monday 3rd November 2025 until 5pm Monday 15th December 2025 for changes to the admission criteria to be implemented for admission from September 2027.
You can access the proposed admission arrangements for Hillingdon community schools for 2027/2028 below.
Summary of proposed changes:
Reduction of Published Admissions Numbers
All community schools have a published admissions number in accordance with the School Admissions Code 2021. This is the number of school places that the admissions authority must off in each relevant age group of a school for which it is the admissions authority.
The Local Authority is consultation to reduce the Published Admissions Number (PAN) for Field End Infant School from 90 to 60, reducing the distance priority radius from 1000m to 750m and if approved, will take affect from September 2027.
The local authority welcomes your feedback. You can access further information regarding the reasoning of proposed changes and make comments or suggestions in response, please visit the Council website via (Consultations and surveys - Hillingdon Council)
Alternatively, you can submit a written response to School Placement and Admissions Team, 2W, High Street, Uxbridge, UB8 1UW
If you have any questions that have not been covered in the consultation document or that are specific to your circumstances and would like to discuss these, please contact admissions@hillingdon.gov.uk / 01895 556644
